state: The target suite is written in full Can, including normal helper functions and the logic choosing scenarios, expectations, retries, cases and outcomes. Can is for machine authors: reliable generation and explicit typed operations matter more than human convenience. Its current proposed executor is TypeScript/Bun generated by trusted reference R, with candidate C isolated from the judge and Go supervisor N outside killable workers. Executable acceptance for R/N and the ordinary-Can ingress route are outstanding. Small host-side research instruments ran under Python with POSIX ownership. Evidence N1: opaque numeric references kept a hostile then getter inert, identity matched, the requested access counted once, and intentional assimilation violated the zero-read expectation. Evidence N2: direct runtime/codec/json.ts::encodeJSON produced [1] from [1n], rejected an array index getter without touching it, and exposed an injected premature accessor read. Generated Can/createCodec wiring and R-run judgment were absent. Evidence F1: separate fd 0 binary and fd 3 UTF-8 channels, present-empty versus absent, timeout on missing EOF, malformed input refusal and nonreader pipe disposal all worked; Go ExtraFiles and the product executable were outside the test. Evidence B1: a real pending Playwright click allowed separate route-token and ping handling; parent resolution produced the marker; a serialized variant stalled. During route-abort disposal that click could fulfill, motivating independent records for input settlement and response effects. Even with the repaired negative-control oracle, browser isolation failed: Chrome caused a macOS Keychain dialog. Its direct headless startup used disposable HOME/profile and loopback CDP but lacked Playwright's pinned --password-store=basic and --use-mock-keychain defaults. Missing switches are a suspected cause without captured process-level attribution. The user canceled that dialog already; owned resources were fully reclaimed. This task authorizes no further browser launch. Future operation requires qualified noninteractive credential behavior, an absence-of-host-UI observation boundary and ownership surviving case/driver loss. Sampling saw 1.72 GiB and 15 browser-related processes, which cannot prove strict resource ceilings. Quick-profile policy is one live case/context, 4 GiB memory, 64 processes and 512 MiB scratch; no strict Mac host enforcement has been accepted. Disk capacity is 256 GB and broad compilation or performance work is still deferred. All integrated N1/N2/B1/F1 checks are unexecuted and migration credit is zero. Review now must produce consistent interfaces and honest implementation dependencies, not promote the research scripts into qualification.

browser_launch.instructions: Select the preferred initial browser startup implementation after considering the prompt incident and independent resource authority.

criteria.driver_launch: Delegate launching to the pinned Playwright implementation within an externally owned N service, registering before effects and preserving test credential settings; record resolved options and require no-host-UI and service-loss qualification.
criteria.direct_launch: Retain a native-parent Chrome exec path whose entire launch configuration is versioned and reconciled with Playwright defaults; separately accept its credential suppression and owned-process cleanup.
criteria.isolated_host: Provision an isolated machine boundary for browser execution before developing its cases, keeping the existing Can API and receipt obligations.

bridge_order.instructions: Choose the planning prerequisite for the still-unproved generated subject ingress.

criteria.gated_lane: Proceed to a dependency plan whose first relevant lane builds only C plus a typed local-realm ingress and establishes R/N acceptance; subsequent native replacements wait for those checks and failures trigger design reconsideration.
criteria.probe_first: Hold off on organizing implementation lanes until a new compiled Can research check is built and run with its necessary compiler, live entry and external parent.
criteria.interpreter_first: Reconsider an entire interpreter backend ahead of planning the candidate bridge.
